newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA says unemployment not due to inflation target.
newsitem.headline: RBA says unemployment not due to inflation target.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) deputy Governor Stephen Grenville said on Monday the central bank's inflation target was not the cause of Australia's high unemployment rate.
He said also he did believe the RBA's dual objective of low inflation and full employment were in conflict.
"I don't think the inflation target is itself the reason for the current unemployment," Grenville told a conference.
Grenville said that since the RBA had begun targeting the underlying rate of inflation in 1993, Australia's growth performance had been good.
The RBA, unlike other other central banks, has mulitiple objectives including those of price stability and maintaining full employment.
"We don't see any contradictions between the two objectives," he said.
Australia's unemployment was at 8.7 percent in March and has been at or above 8.5 percent for the past year.
Grenville also said the RBA would like to see the economy growing at a level consistent with the goal of keeping underlying inflation to between two and three percent over a run of years.
"We would like to see as much growth as the economy can provide while staying in the inflation objective," he said.
